This short, rhythmic verses and the sonorous rhyme of their final words continue throughout the entire surah. In the first verse there are only two words, then the number of words gradually increases, until at the end of the passage the number of words reaches 21, and the words remain majestic and forceful.

"Wal-Tur" (By Mount Tur): Tur refers to a mountain that has trees on it. The clearer view is that it refers to Mount Tur (Koh-e-Tur), which is well known in the story of Hazrat Musa (ʿalayhis-salam), and upon which the tablets of the Torah were revealed. This is because the atmosphere here is one of sacred places, and Allah Ta'ala swears by them, and this oath is also upon a great matter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verses 2–3:

﴿And by a Book inscribed﴾ [52:2] ﴿on parchment unrolled﴾ [52:3]. "By a Book inscribed on thin-leaved parchment." The closer view is that it refers to the Book of Musa (ﷺ... peace be upon him), which was written on tablets. According to this explanation, the connection with Tur is complete. Some commentators have said that it refers to the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz), because after it comes the oath by the Bayt al-Ma'mur, and the oath by the raised canopy (al-Saqf al-Marfu'), and this meaning is also possible.

And the frequented House (by which may be meant the Ka'bah as well, but the clearer view is that it refers to the Bayt al-Ma'mur, the place of worship of the angels), because in authentic hadith, and in the hadith of the Night Journey (isra'), it comes: "Then I was raised to the Bayt al-Ma'mur. That is, these angels worship Allah there, and they circumambulate it just as the people of the earth circumambulate the Ka'bah on earth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 52, verse 5:

And the raised canopy (25:5): "And by the raised canopy." By this is meant the heaven. This is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri, and Abu al-Ahwas has narrated this same opinion from Simak ibn Kharashah ibn 'Ar'arah, who narrated it from Hadrat Ali (karram Allahu wajhahu). Sufyan al-Thawri says that after this, Hadrat Ali (raḍiya Allahu 'anhu) recited this verse:

"And We have made the heaven a protected canopy, yet they turn away from its signs." (cf. Qur'an 21:32)

"And by the sea that is filled (with water)" — that is, the full sea. The sea is mentioned in comparison with the sky because it is very vast; it is full and extensive in breadth and length. It is a sign that contains both beauty and majesty and fear, and it is more instructive together with the other signs mentioned above. The meaning of "al-masjur" is that in which fire has been kindled. In another surah it is said:

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [81:6]

It is also possible that by it is meant (the sea of fire), as in:

﴿And the sea that is set ablaze﴾ [52:6] is meant to be a sea of fire, as in...

"Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur" means an unseen house of worship. By swearing by these great things, the great reality being expressed, and for which the mind has now been prepared, is:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verses 7–8:

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur. None can avert it.﴾

This punishment will certainly come, and no power can prevent it. The impact of these two verses and their rhythmic cadence (saj') are both decisive. The melody of the words also conveys that it will surely occur, that nothing else is possible in it, and that there is no one who can save from it. When this impact falls directly upon the sensitivity of a person's heart, it shakes the heart and transforms its state along with it.

Hafiz Abu Bakr Ibn Abi al-Dunya has related from his father, from Musa ibn Dawud, from Salih al-Mari, from Ja'far ibn Zayd al-Abdi, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) once went out on patrol in Madinah at night. He passed by one of the houses of the Muslims and saw a man standing in prayer. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) stopped and began listening to his recitation. The man began reciting Surah al-Tur. When he reached this point: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur. None can avert it.﴾ Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, this is the truth." Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) dismounted from his donkey, leaned against a wall, sat for some time, and then returned to his home. He remained ill for a full month. People would visit him to inquire after him, but no one knew what illness he had.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) had heard this surah before and had heard it repeatedly. He himself had recited it and led prayers with it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would always recite it in the Maghrib prayer, and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) knew this well, and thus he too would recite this surah in Maghrib, following the example of the Messenger (ﷺ). But on that day its effect upon him was very great, because his heart was open to this impression. His sensibilities on that day were ready to receive influences, so these meanings penetrated his heart and affected him in the manner that this narration indicates, when these verses reached his heart directly with their full weight, full intensity and full reality.

Sometimes such effects fall upon hearts. This is essentially a matter of timing. At a particular moment these impressions sink into the depths of hearts, and they sink in when they directly touch the hearts. In those moments, hearts take these verses from their original source. Just as they had a revelatory impact upon the heart of the Messenger (ﷺ), so they have an impact upon the heart of the listener. Upon the heart of the Messenger (ﷺ) this happened every time, and Allah had granted the heart of the Messenger (ﷺ) this capacity. Sometimes this miraculous effect also falls upon other people, as it fell upon Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Now, after this great and terrifying reality, a terrifying scene:

﴿يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّمَاءُ مَوْرًا﴾ (25 : 9) ﴿وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبَالُ سَيْرًا﴾ (25 : 01). "On the Day when the sky will be violently convulsed, and the mountains will move about in the air."

This sky, which stands still and is built with great firmness, will be struck by sudden agitation and will be tossed about in the manner that waves rise and fall in the sea. These waves move from one place to another and have no stability within them. Then the mountains that stand on this earth, high and firmly rooted, will become so light that they will begin to fly, and all stability and steadiness will be lost from them. This scene is an astonishing and disturbing one, and it points to a dreadful situation in which, if the sky and the mountains themselves are shaken, what can this weak human being hope to remain steady in such a frightful scene and such a terrible situation?

In such frightening and dreadful conditions, the deniers are told something that causes them great fear: that a curse is pronounced on them by Allah, and a curse from Allah is, as it were, a decree of destruction. What was cursed for has, as it were, already occurred. No one can stop Allah from this decision, and it has now come into effect in practice.

﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers, who are playing in their idle talk.﴾ (25:11)
﴿Who are playing in their idle talk.﴾ (25:21)

"Woe on that Day to those who deny, who today are engaged in their disputes as a game." This woe will come on the day when the sky will shake and the mountains will be moving. This is a frightening scene and a frightening destruction. It is the portion of those who deny and who were engrossed in their disputes.

First of all, this description applies to the ideas of the polytheists of Makkah and to their concepts and beliefs, which were extremely superficial and childish. It also applies to the whole life that was founded upon these concepts and beliefs. The Qur'an has commented on this in many places, that it is a game in which there is no seriousness. They are occupied in this game in the way that people enter a pool to bathe and leap and frolic about. Their aim is not to swim in the water toward some goal, or to reach the bank. Their aim is only to leap and frolic in the pool. But the Qur'an applies this word to all ideologies other than Qur'anic ideas, and to all other modes of life other than the Qur'anic way of life, saying that they are a diversion and a game. This is a great truth which the Qur'an has made clear, and only the person who makes a deep study of all ideologies other than Qur'anic ideas can understand it, and he should make this study in the light of the Islamic outlook on life and the Islamic view of the universe. Any deep study will show that the ideas and beliefs of all people are fables. Indeed, even the great philosophies, the great philosophical concepts of human history in which humans take pride, appear to be children's games.

The facts stated in Islamic concepts of life and beliefs, and especially those stated in the Qur'an, have been expressed with great simplicity, strength, clarity and seriousness. All of them are in harmony with human nature, and they accord with human nature without any difficulty, because the Qur'an's study of human nature is extremely realistic. Through it there is also a beautiful explanation of the wonder of the universe, and according to that explanation, its relationship with its Creator is also explained, and all these concepts and explanations are also realistic.

When I read the views of philosophers, I see that the great philosophers, in solving the wonder of this universe, became exhausted and wearied, and they could not give a correct explanation of it, nor could they connect the various facts of the universe with one another. Their ideas appear like a child trying to solve a difficult problem of mathematics. This is because before me there was the Qur'anic solution to this problem, which was clear, plain, easy, natural and appealing, in which there was no crookedness, no complexity and no confusion. The explanation the Qur'an gives of this universe is like the explanation a man gives of machinery he has built. As for the philosophers, they take a few partial facts from this universe and apply them to the whole, and therefore they fail miserably and their concepts fall into contradictions.

When we compare the concepts of these philosophers with the Qur'an, they present a futile game and a clumsy example of confused argument, because Qur'anic ideas are complete, mature, and in accordance with human nature and with reality, and in comparison with the Qur'an their views prove to be immature, impossible and self-contradictory. When a person reads the theories of great philosophers, confusion arises in his concepts about all issues. He is affected by misguided concepts. In reality, these concepts are human efforts to solve the problem of the universe. Then, when a person reflects on the Qur'anic verses that deal with this subject, light gradually enters his mind. His composure and stability return to him. He sees that everything in the universe is placed correctly in its place. Every matter is in its place. Every fact is settled in its place, and there is no disturbance in anything. A person immediately senses that he has reached the truth. He attains rest and tranquility. His heart finds comfort and stability. His intellect becomes satisfied. All kinds of perplexities are removed. All problems are solved, because he has reached a clear truth.

After beliefs, when people build their practical lives upon these beliefs, it becomes apparent that others are engaged in play and frolic, because the priorities of their lives appear, in comparison with Islamic priorities, as childish games. Compared with the lofty priorities that Islam gives to a person, the priorities defined by these other philosophies appear extremely contemptible, trivial and childish. When Islam looks at the occupations of these people, and then sees what importance these occupations hold in their eyes, and when it sees that they are completely immersed in them, and listens to their discussions on this matter, which in their eyes are like people debating a great cosmic problem, Islam, when it casts its gaze upon such people, sees them as children playing in a park with dolls and toys, which they regard as real things, and they behave with these toys as if they were real persons.

Just as Islam gives a sublime and exalted concept of this whole universe, so too it gives a person lofty and exalted priorities within this universe. Islam tells people what the cause and reason for their existence and that of this universe is, and what their end will be. It resolves these questions naturally, so that every person can understand the answer, because these questions arise in the mind of every person: where he came from, why he came, and where he is to go.

The answer that Islam has given to these questions gives a correct conception of its own existence and of the existence of this vast universe spread around it, because man is not something separate from other creatures. He is one creature among those creatures from which other creatures come. He too has come from there. The cause of the existence of all these things is one. Where that other creature goes, he too will go. Therefore Islam's answer is a complete answer, and this universe and man are connected with one another, and all creation is connected with the Creator.

The reflection of the Qur'anic explanation of this universe then falls upon human priorities, and these priorities rise to the level of that concept. Thus, in the consciousness of a Muslim, the priorities of other people appear very contemptible, while he himself, in accordance with his concepts, is occupied with his lofty duties and here acts in accordance with his purpose of existence. In the light of these lofty concepts and lofty priorities, other people appear to a Muslim as engrossed in children's play.

The life of a Muslim is a great life, because his aims are high, and this Muslim is connected with this great universe. He is effective in the existence of this great universe. This reality is more precious than the reality that a person should waste his life in futile and purposeless activities, as other people waste it. In comparison with the priorities of a Muslim, the priorities and occupations of most people appear futile. Woe to those who, merely because of the loftiness of the purposes of life and the loftiness of the concept of this universe, hold concepts about this universe the way children at play do.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verse 13:

﴿On the Day they will be thrust into the fire of Hell with a violent thrust.﴾ (25:31 quoted in the text as: "The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell, being pushed.")

This too is an extremely terrifying scene. Al-da' (الدع) means to push backward. It is a motion that exactly matches the condition of those who hold childish notions about the structure of the universe, who are not serious, and who do not reflect on the affairs happening around them. Thus they will be driven toward Hell, but pushed from behind as well, shoved again and again.

When they are pushed in this manner until they are brought to the very edge of Hell, it will be said:

This is the Urdu-to-English rendering of the passage you provided. The opening citation is Qur'an 25:41 (the passage's reference "25:41" appears in the text), so I have kept it as given.

"This is the Fire which you used to deny." (25:41)

These people will still be in that state, pushed from one side to another towards the Fire, helpless and overpowered. Then, as a rebuke and reprimand, it will be said to them. A reference will be made to their past.

﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾ (25:51)

These people used to say in this world about the Quran that it is magic. It is said here in mockery: is this fire also merely magic, or is it a reality, and a terrifying reality? Or the situation is that you do not see this fire in the same way you did not see the Quran.

When this mocking rebuke and chastisement ends, they are swiftly brought to despair of seriousness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verse 16:

"Enter it (the Fire) and burn; whether you are patient or impatient, it is the same for you. You are being recompensed only for what you used to do." (Qur'an 52:16, as quoted in the commentary, cited here as 25:61 in the source)

What greater wretchedness could there be than this: whether one is patient or not, the punishment will continue, and no one will be there to stop it. If one endures, the pain is the same; if one does not, the pain is the same. Dwelling in Hell is one's destiny, whether one screams or falls silent. This is because in this world, reward and punishment depend on deeds, and what has already happened cannot be changed or altered. With these words, this scene now ends, and with it this first part also ends.

The second part of this surah is also thought-provoking, but in it there is gentleness, ease, and comfort, especially after the previous scene, in which severe punishment was mentioned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verses 17–18:

This scene lies close to the blessings that had been settled in the consciousness of the people addressed from the very beginning. Therefore, in terms of its purity and its appeal to the senses, it is very attractive to people, and these scenes stand directly opposite to, and in contrast with, the harsh and terrifying punishment presented earlier concerning the dry and childish hearts.

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and springs, enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord will protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire.﴾ (Qur'an 52:17–18 as quoted by the commentator; the passage cited here is 25:81 in the original text) Being saved from that Fire, whose scenes have just been presented, is itself a great success, and here there are blessings along with that protection. The Jannat al-Na'im (Gardens of Delight) are also with them; there they will derive pleasure from the blessings of Allah.

The Jannat al-Na'im (Gardens of Delight) are also with them; there they will derive pleasure from the blessings of Allah.

With these blessings and pleasures, there is also a welcome and honour.

﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction, as a reward for what you used to do﴾ (52:19). That they will be called out to from the higher realm is itself an exalted rank and an honour, and it will be said that they deserve it.

Reclining on couches arranged in rows, facing one another (25:02)... These couches will be placed face to face, in a very fine arrangement, and beyond other delights they will meet their brethren.

And We will wed them to huris with beautiful, wide eyes (25:02). This is a supreme blessing, the like of which a human being can imagine.

Now this honour goes one step further. Their believing offspring are also joined with them, and they too share in these blessings; and these are additional favours upon them. Although the deeds of the offspring may be less than those of these God-conscious people in standing, yet if the offspring is a believer, they will be joined with their fathers, and there will be no diminution in the ranks of the fathers. Each person there will be responsible for and deserving of his own deeds. This principle remains in its place, but it will be by the grace of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verses 21–22:

﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.﴾ (52:21)

This scene continues. The blessings of Paradise are being described. These blessings are of many kinds: fruits are coming, meats of every variety are coming, and they will be passing to one another cups of wine, whatever they desire. This wine will not be like the wine of the world, after drinking which people either indulge in idle and abusive talk or commit indecent acts. Rather, it will be a purified and pure wine.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verses 25–27:**

"We used to pray to Him before this. Indeed, He is the Most Good and the Most Merciful" (﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ ۖ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ (25:82)). Here the people of the Garden said that in their earlier life they used to call upon Allah and knew His attributes: that He is al-Barr (the Most Good) and al-Azim (the Mighty).

"Indeed, He is the Most Good and the Most Merciful." This is the secret of how these people reached Paradise. They engaged in this discourse, and these successful people are truly honoured persons in the Gardens of Bliss (Dar al-Na'im).

In the first section of this surah we clearly came to know what the punishment of Allah will be, and in the second section we came to know about the blessings of Allah. In this way, our awareness for grasping the realities became very sharp. Accordingly, the discourse begins, with great speed, in short sentences and forceful words, to present the realities before the veil of human perception. The whisperings that arise within the soul are pursued, and these realities are conveyed to the human mind through questions, which have the tone of rebuke and challenge and are very forceful. Before these questions and challenges, a person cannot stand firm.

The Prophet ﷺ is being guided that he should continue to remind (the people), and that he should not be affected by their evil talk, and should pay no heed to the accusations they are making. At times they would charge that he is a "kahin" (soothsayer), and at other times they would say that he is mad (majnun). Thus they would level accusations that were well known among them: that soothsayers and madmen receive guidance from the devils, and that the devils afflict certain people with madness and make them majnun. In their view, Satan was at work behind both of these qualities, and for this reason they would lay these accusations upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Then they would charge the Prophet ﷺ with being a sorcerer (sahir) and a magician. They made this charge because they were astonished before the eloquent and elegant style of the Holy Qur'an. This Qur'an was such a miracle that they had neither seen nor heard speech of this kind. Meanwhile, they considered themselves masters of speech. Yet, because of their spiritual disease, these people were determined not to accept the Qur'an as the word of Allah, and so they were compelled to offer some explanation or other about this speech. Sometimes they would say that jinn teach the Messenger this speech; that he is a soothsayer who takes this speech from the jinn; or that he is a magician who learns magic from the jinn; or that he is a poet and that jinn cast ideas upon him; or that he is mad and Satan has touched him and makes him say these strange things.

These statements are extremely false, wicked, shameful, and distressing. But Allah consoles His Messenger ﷺ, assuring him that he should not pay the slightest heed to them. Upon you is the grace and bounty (of your Lord). You are neither a soothsayer nor a madman.

﴿فَمَا أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Tur 52:29] "By the grace of your Lord, you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman." After this, strong disapproval is expressed of their claim that these people charge the Messenger ﷺ with being a poet.

Am yaqooloon ........ al-manoon (25:03) "Do they say, 'He is a poet, for whom we are waiting for the turns of time'?" They said this. They would console one another in this way, that is, "Be patient against this movement and remain steadfast in your religion. At his appointed time this man will die, and thus we will be rid of him." They would say to one another, "Be patient, for he will die." This is why the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told to say to them in a threatening manner, "Very well."

Say: "Wait, and I too am waiting along with you"; "and you will soon know who has the good end and who attains victory and success."

The leaders of Quraysh were called *dhawu al-ahlam* (those of sound judgment), with the implication that they were very wise and conducted affairs with great prudence. The Qur'an addresses them with a serious mockery of this supposed wisdom: their conduct is entirely contrary to reason and intelligence. It is asked: is their opinion about Hazrat Muhammad, and their denial of revelation and prophethood, a sign of that wisdom? Rather, they are rebellious, and they turn away from the very thing their own reason accepts.

Am taʾmuruhum ahlamuhum bihadha am hum qawmun taghun (Is it their intellects that bid them to this, or are they a people transgressing beyond bounds?) [Qur'an 52:32, quoted here in the commentary as 25:23 in the Urdu source's reference]. In the first question there is mockery, and in the second an accusation of base conduct, and one of these two charges fits the position these people take.

Their tongues were so insolent toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they alleged he composes this speech of his own accord. A question is put to this as well, expressing disapproval. If they say such things, they should not say them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 52, verse 33:

Am yaqooloona taqawwalah (25:33): "Do they say that he has fabricated it himself?" And immediately after this, the real truth is laid bare.

Bal la yu'minoon (25:33): "The truth is that they do not want to believe." Their hearts have not attained the awareness of faith. It is this lack of awareness that prompts them to say such a thing, and they say it only because they are deprived of the blessing of faith. If they were to grasp the reality of the Qur'an, they would know that it is not the speech of a human being, and that the one who brought it is truthful and trustworthy.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 52, verse 34:

﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful.﴾ (25:43 is cited in the Urdu text as the challenge: "If they are truthful in their claim, let them produce a speech of this same quality.") The challenge has been repeated again and again in the Qur'an, and the deniers have been unable to accept it; indeed they have remained utterly helpless. In the same way, people will remain unable to meet it until the Day of Resurrection. The Qur'an has a secret: whoever reads its verses for the first time finds in them every distinctive quality, whether or not he knows the reasons for its inimitability. He senses that the Qur'anic text has a particular power. It is clearly apparent that, beyond its meanings and modes of expression, there is something special in the Qur'an. As soon as one hears the Qur'an, this quality affects the mind. Some people perceive it clearly, while others perceive it somewhat vaguely and obscurely, but every person senses it. What is this quality of the Qur'an, and what is its source? It is difficult to determine. Is this effect due to the meanings of the Qur'an, or to the forms and scenes of the Qur'an, or is it an effect of its wording, in that there is a difference between it and other speech made from the same language, or do all these elements together provide its inimitability, or is it something that transcends even these?

This is a secret hidden in every Qur'anic verse. Whoever reads the Qur'anic verses senses this secret. Afterwards, each person seeks its mysteries and subtleties according to his own conjecture, and these become known through reflection and contemplation, and they are present throughout the whole Qur'an.

For example, this inimitability exists in terms of the complete and correct conception that the Qur'an gives to reason and intellect: the conception of the reality of human existence, the conception of existence in this universe, and the conception of that "primary" Reality from which all realities flow, namely the conception of Allah.

Then there is inimitability also in its method and style, by which the Qur'an builds human concepts. The Qur'an addresses human beings in a natural manner, and its mode of address is also distinctive. This manner is not found in the human styles of speech of all languages. The Qur'an turns the human heart and intellect in every direction. It seeks to introduce sound ideas from every side, and it deals with human beings in the way that a fully aware Being deals with someone.

The guidance that the Qur'an gives possesses a remarkable comprehensiveness, balance and complete harmony, and this whole discourse is of one level and one standard. This is by no means found in human speech. Human speech does not remain in one state, does not stay on one level, and cannot maintain a standard in every respect; and establishing balance is simply impossible for it, such that there is no excess in any matter, no defect, no excess or deficiency, and complete harmony, and no contradiction or conflict anywhere in the speech, neither in its principles nor in its branches.

These outward matters, which can be perceived, together with that hidden miraculous effect which no one can deny, are proofs that this is miraculous speech, and these things together give the Qur'an the quality of inimitability. The inimitability of the Qur'an is something that no person, whose senses are sound, who is honest, who is truth-seeking, and who studies the Qur'an with strength, depth and clarity, and studies the Qur'anic text with a sound heart, can now produce speech like.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verse 35:

﴿أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ﴾ (52:35) "Were they created by nothing, or are they the creators?" Their existence without any cause is contrary to the logic of nature, and this point needs no lengthy or brief debate. As for the claim that they are the creators of themselves, no one has ever asserted it, nor did those people hold it. If both of these notions are contrary to natural reasoning, then the third possibility remains, the one the Qur'an points to: that they are all creatures of Allah, and in this creation Allah has no partner. Therefore, in lordship, worship and obedience, Allah has no partner either. This is a very simple and natural truth.

Let their outlook be turned briefly toward the heavens: did they create this vast universe? The universe itself is not its own creator, just as they are not the creators of their own selves.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 52, verses 36–37:

Am khuliqu ........ yuqinun (25:63): "Or were they created by nothing, or are they themselves the creators?" [Qur'an 52:35]. "Rather, they do not have certainty" (25:63). These people, and every intelligent person who thinks in a natural manner, cannot be convinced that the earth and the heavens created themselves, or came into being without a Creator, or were created by themselves, that is, by some human being. These are questions that everyone must answer. Their condition was such that when they were asked this question, they would say that Allah created them. But this reality was not so clear in their perception that it would bring about any change in their hearts, their thinking and their conduct, or that they would adopt any definite belief.

Bal la yuqinun (25:63): "Rather, they do not have certainty." Now, descending a little from creation, a question of lesser rank is put to them: Come, you are not the creators of this universe, so are you the custodians of the treasures of the earth? Do you have authority over the affairs of people? It is Allah alone who gives little to one and much to another. He alone is the Administrator and the Disposer of affairs, and this interpretation is the one that can be acted upon and is convincing. It is according to the situation that prevails in this world: when neither are they the owners of the treasures of Allah nor do the affairs of the earth lie in their power, then who other than Allah is there?

Now, descending one step further, they are addressed: Do you not regard the Qur'an as coming from Allah? If so, do you have any means of access to Allah by which you have come to know that the Qur'an is not from Him?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verse 38:

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen in on the higher realm? Then let the one who listens in bring a clear authority.﴾ (25:83)

Muhammad (ﷺ) claims that he is the Messenger of Allah, that revelation comes to him, and that this Qur'an was sent down from Allah, and these people deny it. Do they have a means of knowing the affairs of the higher realm, so that Muhammad (ﷺ) would not be receiving revelation and the truth would be something else? Therefore, let anyone who has such a means of listening in bring a proof: a proof that possesses its own power, such that a person is compelled to affirm it. This alludes to the proofs that the Qur'an provides, which are in fact a clear authority (sultan mubin), and which immediately take hold of the heart and mind. In the face of them, these people act with obstinacy and stubbornness.

Now we take up their saying about Allah, that the angels are the daughters of Allah. This address is directed straight to the polytheists of Makkah, and it is for the purpose of shaming and humiliating them even further.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verse 39:

﴿Am lahu al-banat wa lakum al-banun﴾ (25:93): "Has He daughters while you have sons?" In their view, daughters were a lesser kind of creature than sons. So much so that when someone was told that a daughter had been born to him, his face would turn black from grief, anguish and displeasure. Yet despite these beliefs, they felt no shame in attributing daughters to Allah. Here Allah objects to them according to their own customs and practices, so that they might feel some shame at this claim, even though their own view was also mistaken and in need of correction.

The Prophet (ﷺ) would invite them to Islam. They considered this a great burden, although he gave the invitation purely for the sake of Allah. He did not ask for any reward, nor did he wish to impose any tax upon them. They should have been grateful to him for this free instruction, and if they did not accept it, they should at least have declined it in a gentlemanly manner. Therefore, their attitude was entirely unjustified.

Do you ask them for any payment, that they are burdened with a debt they cannot bear? (Surah At-Tur 52:40, as quoted at the opening of this passage, with its wording taken from the commentary's own citation.)

Rather, the meaning is that they cannot bear the financial burden you would place upon them. So if the reality is that no wage is being sought and no burden is being laid on them, then how base and humiliating is your attitude? Should you not feel ashamed of your conduct?

After this, the present state of these people, both in their own existence and in this universe, is set before them once again: they are servants, and they have limits. Many matters in this universe are hidden from them, and only a few are known to them. All the secrets belong to the Lord of this universe alone, and He alone knows them. The realm of the unseen is very vast, and they cannot enter into it, because they are servants.

Am 'indahum... yaktubun (52:41): "Or do they have the unseen, so that they are writing [it down]?" (cf. 25:14)

They know that they do not possess knowledge of the unseen, nor are they writing from knowledge of the unseen, nor do they have the power to write decisions in the unseen realm. It is Allah who writes the destinies of His servants in the books of the unseen.

The One who knows the unseen is the only One who can manage affairs and decree destinies. They cannot make any decision, because they do not know the unseen and cannot inscribe anything in the storehouses of the unseen. Therefore they can do nothing against you. These people can neither exercise any control over your future, nor can they plot any scheme.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 52, verse 42:

Am yureedoona ........ al-makeedoon (25:24) ["Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve, it is they who will be ensnared by the plot."] Is it that they want to devise a scheme? If that is so, then the scheme will recoil upon those who disbelieve. That is, Allah, who knows the unseen, will encompass them with His own plan, and Allah's plans will fall upon them, for Allah is the best of planners.

The passage is labelled as commentary on verse 52:43, but the verse references inside it are 25:34, and I have translated the text exactly as given.

Am lahum ilahun ghayrullah (25:34) "Or do they have a deity other than Allah" who can protect them and who will save them from the punishment of Allah?

Subhanallahi 'amma yushrikun (25:34) "Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him." The notions they hold about Allah are false.

This attack on shirk now concludes. It was a systematic assault, each step built upon the one before, and every sentence of it had a very great effect. In this assault, all their doubts, all their arguments, and all their ideas were refuted, and they were rendered helpless. It was thereby established that these people are deniers of the truth, obstinate, doubters of clear truth, and clingers to far-fetched doubts. Indeed, these people are being stubborn and obstinate.

﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling, they would say, "It is but layered clouds."﴾ (25:44). The meaning is this: if a punishment were sent upon them, and they saw it coming down like a fragment of the sky about to fall upon them, and they were about to be destroyed by it, they would still say "sahab markum" (that it is a cloud gathering and advancing), and that there is water in it which will be a means of life for them. They would say this out of obstinacy. In no way will they accept the truth, even if the sword is hanging over their heads.

This points to the story of the people of 'Ad, when they saw the storm of wind and rain approaching and said, ﴿This is a cloud that will bring us rain.﴾ (46:24). They were given this answer: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were seeking to hasten: a wind containing a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord.﴾ (46:24)

After this portrayal of their hostility and obstinacy, even if punishment comes upon them like a sword hanging over their heads, the address now turns back to the Prophet (ﷺ). The purpose is that he should disregard their affair and leave them to face the end mentioned at the beginning of this surah. A punishment from Allah, one more severe than the other, awaits them. Wait for the command of Allah, which is mighty, and which is the guardian of you and watches over you at all times. Glorify your Lord with His praise: when you rise in the morning, and when you rise at night, and at the time when the stars set.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verses 45–47:

This is a fresh critical attack on the opponents. It begins with a severe threat and warning: when the Trumpet is blown, all of these people will be destroyed, and this event will take place somewhat before the resurrection, the gathering and the raising up. On that day, none of their schemes will avail them. Today these people do devise some plans against the Islamic movement, but on that day no plan of theirs will avail them. Even before the Hereafter, a punishment is about to come upon them, but they do not know it.

After this final warning, this attack on the deniers (mukadhdhibin) comes to an end. Earlier, this surah pursued them thoroughly and launched fierce assaults upon them, and at the end it declared that a near punishment awaits them and a distant punishment also awaits them. Now the address turns to the Prophet ﷺ, against whom the wrongdoers committed injustice and fabricated all kinds of statements. He is instructed to be patient. These difficulties are going to be removed. These deniers themselves are about to face the punishment. The path of da'wah (the call to Islam) is difficult and long, and patience alone is the method of da'wah upon it. The outcome should be left to Allah, for the decision is His alone.

After this final warning, this attack on the deniers (mukadhdhibin) comes to an end. Earlier, this surah pursued them thoroughly and launched fierce assaults upon them, and at the end it declared that a near punishment awaits them and a distant punishment also awaits them. Now the address turns to the Prophet ﷺ, against whom the wrongdoers committed injustice and fabricated all kinds of statements. He is instructed to be patient. These difficulties are going to be removed. These deniers themselves are about to face the punishment. The path of da'wah (the call to Islam) is difficult and long, and patience alone is the method of da'wah upon it. The outcome should be left to Allah, for the decision is His alone.

Along with the command to be patient, you are also given a verbal honour. You are deemed worthy of Allah's favour. You are given such affection that, through this gentle touch of love, all your pain and weariness are removed, and you are told that patience in the face of hardships is a matter that is very beloved and pleasing to Allah, and that this is the means and the connection to that honour.

﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord, for you are within Our sight﴾ (25:84). This is a beautiful expression, a finest picture, and a great honour.

This is a station of honour that no human being has reached. Throughout the Qur'an this station is not shown in such a beautiful manner, and even in the instructions given to other prophets, there is no expression as beautiful as this one.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 52, verse 49:

Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) was told: "And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed to you." It was also said:

"And I cast upon you a love from Me, so that you might be reared under My eye." Elsewhere it was said:

"And I have made you for Myself." All these expressions show that the rank of Musa (peace be upon him) was extremely exalted. However, the words used for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are these:

"Indeed, you are before Our eyes" (25:84 — "فانک باعیننا"), meaning "you are in Our sight." This is a manner of speech in which special honour is evident. Special love is evident. It contains colours that are extremely subtle and beautiful. A human being is incapable of presenting such expressions. For us it is sufficient that we live within these colours, and we merely point towards them.

The method of constant connection with this love is then taught:

"And glorify your Lord with His praise when you arise, and glorify Him during the night and at the setting of the stars" (52:48–49, cited here as 25:94 in the source) — "تم جب اٹھو تو اپنے رب کی حمد کے ساتھ تسبیح کرو ، رات کو بھی اس کی تسبیح کیا کرو اور ستارے جب پلٹتے ہیں اس وقت بھی۔"

These are the times: day and night, upon rising from sleep, during the night, and in the morning when the stars set. These are the moments in which benefit may be gained from this bond of love. The glorification of Allah is a provision for the journey. It is the love of God and the supplication of hearts; then, when it comes from a heart that loves, what more can be said?
